verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents its own local development runner, explicitly not for production use, which gives a develop-and-test surface separate from production deployment. However, no hosted Pipecat Cloud sandbox or test mode is documented, and Evals run against the real agent with the same services, so isolation from production data is not shown. This is a separate local environment rather than a true sandbox; mock-generation from the OpenAPI spec is only a developer building block and earns no credit. missing for 10: a documented sandbox or test mode in Pipecat Cloud, a guarantee that test runs are isolated from production data or services, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The development runner is a local development tool — it isn't built or supported for production use
Pipecat ships a built-in development runner (pipecat.runner.run) that handles the server-side glue most bots need during development
